name: Lumen
evidence_summary: Lumen source evidences fully managed or co-managed SD-WAN for enterprise.
cost_model: Quote-based; Lumen states fully managed or co-managed SD-WAN, with access/network services priced by requirement.
key_differentiators: Fully managed or co-managed SD-WAN with strong NaaS positioning and integrated network services.
Substantial underlay ownership in North America with global reach.
Co-managed model provides operational flexibility for customers wanting selective control.
best_fit_for: North American enterprises wanting integrated managed SD-WAN, access and broader network services from one provider.
Buyers attracted to the NaaS consumption model.
Organisations wanting genuine co-managed delivery rather than pure managed or pure DIY.
watch_outs: SASE and security capabilities are largely partner-integrated rather than native; the SSE platform choice needs explicit evaluation.
International delivery depth is less prominent than the dedicated global carriers.
Underlying SD-WAN platform should be confirmed; platform choice affects feature set.
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: Depends on platform (VeloCloud, Versa); Lumen portal analytics for managed customers.

resilience.note: Extensive owned fibre and PoP diversity across North America.

profile.platform_architecture: Lumen operates one of the largest fibre backbones in North America with extensive owned conduit and metro assets, delivering managed SD-WAN on a multi-vendor bench (VeloCloud, Versa, Cisco and Fortinet). Edge computing assets place compute close to enterprise sites. Following the EMEA business sale to Colt, Lumen's centre of gravity is firmly the Americas.
profile.security_sase: Managed SASE pairs the SD-WAN bench with partner SSE platforms plus Lumen security services including DDoS mitigation at backbone scale and Black Lotus Labs threat intelligence, which is well regarded. Security depth follows the chosen platform with credible carrier SOC operations behind it.
profile.service_support_channel: Fully managed and co-managed models with 24x7 operations and named service management. US enterprise and public sector delivery is the strength; UK and European delivery now routes substantially via partners post-divestment, so confirm in-region arrangements during procurement.
profile.commercials_verdict: Per-site managed pricing, quote based, often sharp where Lumen fibre is on-net. The Netify verdict: shortlist Lumen for US-weighted estates, especially where on-net fibre, DDoS scale or edge compute matter. For UK and Europe-led procurement, Lumen's divested EMEA position moves regional rivals ahead.

vendor_faqs.a: Lumen's threat research team, with visibility drawn from one of the internet's largest backbones. Its intelligence feeds Lumen security services including DDoS mitigation and adds genuine signal to managed security offers.

vendor_faqs.q: How does Lumen serve UK sites now?
vendor_faqs.a: Primarily through partner networks following the EMEA sale to Colt. UK sites can still sit in a Lumen-managed global estate; validate in-region delivery, support paths and SLAs explicitly in any RFP.

vendor_faqs.q: When is Lumen the value pick?
vendor_faqs.a: When your sites are on or near Lumen fibre in North America: on-net economics, backbone DDoS protection and edge compute make the bundle hard to beat for US-centric estates.

shortlist_summary: Lumen offer fully managed or co-managed SD-WAN with NaaS positioning and integrated network services, framing the proposition as a longer-term network programme rather than a point SD-WAN deployment. Typically shortlisted by organisations thinking about longer-term infrastructure strategy rather than a tactical overlay, particularly where integrating a broader set of network services under a single provider is part of the requirement.
cost_note: Per-site managed; sharp where Lumen fibre is on-net in the US, premium elsewhere.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US); UK delivery is largely via partners following the EMEA divestment to Colt.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: Scale and enhance your WAN while you minimize risk using fully managed or co-managed SD-WAN solutions for enterprise.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Corroborated by the SASE page, which states that pro-managed service provides a fully managed Lumen SASE solution including design, implementation and support for the entire term of the service, and by the Cisco Meraki product page which states Lumen fully manages the solution from design to installation and Day 2 management of all devices. Lumen designs, deploys, monitors and supports end to end, although the underlying SD-WAN and SASE software is Versa, Fortinet or Cisco technology.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: The SD-WAN Service is offered as a managed or co-managed service.
f03_co_managed_service.note: The SD-WAN and Managed Equipment Service Guide adds that for Managed Equipment and SD-WAN with Meraki, Lumen provides read-only access credentials and co-management with read-write access is only available with Lumen approval, so the shared-rights model is real but gated.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. Checked the SD-WAN and SASE product pages, the SD-WAN service schedule, the SASE service guide, the SD-WAN and Managed Equipment service guide and the docs.lumen.com SD-WAN with Versa portal documentation; none describes tenant isolation, delegated administration, branded portals or templates letting managed service providers operate the platform under their own brand. Searches for a Lumen white-label or wholesale SD-WAN programme returned only unrelated third-party vendors. Absence of evidence is not being graded as absence of capability.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: Standard Implementation includes (a) responsibility for roll-out schedule, installation management, and project communication
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: The SASE service guide adds that the customer may purchase additional add-on services from Lumen to support design, implementation and management, and the Cisco Meraki page describes a service wrapper covering design, deployment, configuration and site activation. Explicit migration runbooks, pilots, rollback plans and training were not found by name in the documents reviewed, so this rests on the structured design and implementation wrap rather than on a documented migration methodology.

f07_lifecycle_management.quote: Lifecycle management – notification of end of sale/end of support.
f07_lifecycle_management.note: The same service guide lists CPE break/fix (RMA) warranty support for failed devices and processing of return material authorisation replacement requests, plus patch management for all hardware and software. The SD-WAN service schedule states that during the initial service term purchased CPE is eligible for the Managed Device Replacement Service Level in the Lumen Service Level Agreement, so replacement is contractual rather than best effort.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: Cellular back-up access service leverages third party cellular network connectivity and is established utilizing CPE (internal modem or an external enterprise-class cellular-to-Ethernet bridge)
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: Graded partial because the contractual wording covers cellular as back-up only and rides third-party cellular networks rather than Lumen SIMs. The Cisco Meraki product page mentions support for connectivity options including built-in LTE. No mention of 5G specifically, of SIM management, or of signal monitoring was found in the SD-WAN service schedule, the SD-WAN and Managed Equipment service guide, the SASE service guide or the docs.lumen.com Versa documentation.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: The Sovereign SASE solution is deployed on dedicated SASE gateways in Lumen's global points of presence (PoPs) or on customer premises, based on the customer's preference and needs.
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: The PoPs are Lumen's own, which is what this field measures, and the SASE product page advertises 50+ low-latency edge nodes in key metro areas. The security software running in them is Versa or Fortinet technology, which does not change the ownership of the infrastructure. One complication is recorded in conflicts: the SASE service guide also describes an option delivered through a global network of VMware SASE points of presence, which would be partner_integrated rather than Lumen-owned.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.quote: The Lumen SD-WAN with Versa Networks network Controllers are hosted within Lumen facilities, but can also be deployed as private infrastructure in a customer provided environment for an additional charge.
f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Reinforced by the dated May 2024 Versa Sovereign SASE press release, which states the solution is deployed on dedicated SASE gateways in Lumen's global PoPs or on customer premises based on the customer's preference and needs. Customer-hosted, dedicated and sovereign options are therefore documented, not only shared multi-tenant locations.

f21_private_global_backbone.quote: Black Lotus Labs, Lumen's threat research team, leverages its unique visibility into Lumen's global internet backbone using ML algorithms to generate threat intelligence
f21_private_global_backbone.note: Lumen owns and operates its own global backbone, which is the substance of this field. Confidence is medium rather than high for two reasons: the clearest wording found is incidental to a threat intelligence sentence, and the most explicit owned-fibre statement found, that Lumen operates the largest ultra-low-loss intercity fiber network in North America, is scoped to North America. No page reviewed states as a product property that inter-region SASE or SD-WAN traffic rides the Lumen backbone rather than the public internet.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: Lumen offers Service Availability Service Levels for Qualifying Services based on the following Availability Tiers.
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: The published Lumen Service Level Agreement names Lumen SD-WAN Service with Versa Networks, Lumen SD-WAN Service with Cisco Meraki and Lumen SASE Solutions as qualifying services, and carries availability tiers, a four hour incident response commitment, managed device replacement targets, and regional latency, jitter and packet delivery objectives. These are credit-bearing contractual commitments rather than best-effort targets.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Next Generation Firewall (NGFW) is available as a service license with Fortinet and is powered by FortiOS
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: The firewall function is Fortinet technology licensed and operated by Lumen, so partner_integrated rather than yes. The same guide describes anti-malware, web filtering and firewall, intrusion detection and prevention (IDS/IPS) within the unified threat management set, and the SD-WAN service schedule describes a Security Upgrade providing a set of firewall, web filtering and intrusion prevention. The function is integrated into the delivered platform, but the technology belongs to another vendor.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: intrusion detection and prevention (IDS/IPS), and data loss prevention
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: DLP is listed on the Lumen SASE product page as one of the Security Service Edge services alongside NGFW, SWG, ZTNA and CASB, and appears in the SASE service guide within the Fortinet-powered feature set, so it is another vendor's engine operated by Lumen. No Lumen page reviewed describes content classification detail, blocking versus flagging behaviour, alerting or exception workflows, so confidence is medium on the depth of the capability rather than on its presence.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: Lumen resources are available 24x7 for support.
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: Graded partial for two reasons. First, the SD-WAN and Managed Equipment service guide evidences 24x7x365 performance management by Lumen skilled operations engineers and continuous network monitoring, which covers the NOC half, but the SASE service guide states that the Pro-Managed service does not include security operations center services, so the SOC half is not part of the standard managed wrap. Second, no source reviewed documents ownership of incidents through to root cause analysis, structured service reviews or change governance as contractual elements; those terms were searched for in both service guides and the service schedule and not found.

delivery_model.quote: Scale and enhance your WAN while you minimize risk using fully managed or co-managed SD-WAN solutions for enterprise.
delivery_model.note: Lumen operates the service rather than authoring the SD-WAN or SASE software. Its own SASE page names Fortinet and Versa as the underlying technology partners, and the SD-WAN service schedule names Versa Networks and Cisco Meraki. Lumen does own and author the underlying network, but the SASE and SD-WAN products themselves are partner technology operated by Lumen.

underlay_ownership.quote: operates the largest ultra-low-loss intercity fiber network in North America
underlay_ownership.note: Lumen owns extensive fibre and core routing of its own, evidenced by the dated September 2025 network expansion release. At the same time its SD-WAN product page states the service connects branch and remote users using MPLS, broadband or Wi-Fi, and the SD-WAN service schedule states cellular back-up leverages third party cellular network connectivity, so third-party and customer-supplied access is routinely used alongside owned circuits. Hence mixed rather than owns_own_circuits.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Choose flexible pro‑ or self‑managed options from industry‑leading partners Fortinet and Versa.
sse_layer_ownership.note: Fortinet and Versa, with VMware appearing as a third stack. The SASE service guide confirms the NGFW is available as a service licence with Fortinet powered by FortiOS and names FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiEMS and FortiClient, and the dated May 2024 press release describes Lumen SASE powered by Versa technology. The same guide also references a VMware SASE PoP-based delivery option. Lumen did not build the SSE stack; it operates and wraps partner technology on its own network.

regulatory_documentation.quote: The SOC 2 program provides customer assurance of the Lumen controls supporting the AICPA Trust Services criteria relevant to security, availability, and confidentiality (where applicable).
regulatory_documentation.note: Named on Lumen's trust centre compliance and audit page: ISO 27001, SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI-DSS attestations of compliance, HIPAA, a NIST federal controls assessment confirmation letter and the SIG questionnaire, with covered services listed per attestation and reference to the SSAE 18 and ISAE 3402 standards. Not found on the pages reviewed: NHS DSPT, DORA, NIS2. Note that SOC 2 scope is named against specific services such as Adaptive Network Security, Colocation Services, Edge Compute Platform and Technology Solution Services rather than against SD-WAN or SASE Solutions by name.

pop_count.quote: 50+ low‑latency edge nodes in key metro areas
pop_count.note: Confidence is low because Lumen publishes two different figures for the same concept and neither is labelled a SASE PoP count. The main SASE product page states 50+ low-latency edge nodes in key metro areas, while the Lumen SASE Solutions FAQ states 60+ edge locations in major metros connected to high-capacity fiber. Graded from the product page as the more current supplier-controlled surface, with the disagreement recorded in conflicts. The quote contains a non-breaking hyphen character in low-latency as rendered on the page.

sla_availability_pct.quote: 99.99% availability SLA for single device; 100% service availability when purchases in High Availability configuration
sla_availability_pct.note: This is the only Lumen page found stating an availability percentage for SD-WAN in prose. The contractual Lumen Service Level Agreement expresses availability as tiers in a table rather than as one figure: Platinum Managed Service 100%, Platinum 99.999%, Gold 99.99%, Silver 99.9%, Bronze 99.5%, with the applicable tier depending on the qualifying service ordered. So 99.99 is the single-device SD-WAN figure, not a portfolio-wide number, and 100% applies only in a high availability configuration.

sectors.healthcare.quote: Moving into the future of healthcare with network modernization
sectors.healthcare.note: Dedicated healthcare industry page carrying four named customers: VSP Vision, American Family Care, Society of Diagnostic Medical Sonography and Accolade. The Accolade entry is explicitly SD-WAN attributed and is also featured on the main SD-WAN product page, so the sector evidence connects directly to the product under comparison rather than to Lumen's general portfolio. The quoted string is the American Family Care story headline. Note that other headlines on this page use a non-breaking hyphen in 'SD-WAN', so the hyphen-free quote was chosen deliberately for re-verification.

sectors.financial_services.quote: Expanding connectivity and security to minimize downtime and reduce TCO
sectors.financial_services.note: Dedicated financial services industry page naming Certegy Payment Solutions, Horizon Bank, Euromoney and SELCO Community Credit Union, with explicit SASE and SD-WAN blocks. The quoted string is the Horizon Bank story headline. Separately, the SD-WAN product page features CURE Auto Insurance under 'Ensuring business continuity during digital transformation', giving a second insurance-side data point tied directly to SD-WAN.

sectors.retail_ecommerce.quote: Transforming retail with fast, flexible connectivity
sectors.retail_ecommerce.note: The strongest sector evidence in this assessment. Retail is the only sector with a dedicated SASE data sheet ('Lumen SASE Solutions for the Retail Industry', source 4), which is sector-specific collateral for the exact product under comparison, and it is backed by a dedicated retail industry page naming CITY Furniture, Micro Center, Space Needle and VSP Vision. The quoted string is the CITY Furniture story headline. The retail data sheet also carries the claim '98% of retailers surveyed currently use or plan to migrate their legacy network to SD-WAN in the next two years', which is an unattributed vendor survey stat and was not relied on.

sectors.manufacturing.quote: Enhancing network performance for a cleaner world.
sectors.manufacturing.note: Dedicated manufacturing industry page with four named customers: Upstate Niagara Cooperative, alphabroder, VSP Vision and Calgon Carbon, plus explicit SASE and SD-WAN blocks. The quoted string is the Calgon Carbon story headline. Caveat worth recording for the buyer: the named customers skew to food co-operative, apparel distribution and activated carbon rather than heavy discrete manufacturing or OT/ICS environments, so this is not evidence of industrial control network capability.

sectors.energy_utilities.quote: Lumen IT solutions help some of the top global energy providers, offshore drilling companies and utility giants navigate change
sectors.energy_utilities.note: Deliberately graded down from 'yes'. Lumen does maintain a dedicated energy and utilities industry page, which on a literal reading of the grading rule would qualify as 'yes'. It was not graded that way because the page contains no named customer, no case study, and no SD-WAN or SASE content beyond one generic sentence pairing DIA with SASE. The quoted claim about 'top global energy providers' is unattributed and names nobody. This is the sector named in a page with nothing behind it for the product under comparison, which is the definition of 'partial'. If a named energy SD-WAN or SASE customer surfaces later this should move to 'yes'.

sectors.government_public_sector.quote: EIS is one of the transformation contracts from the General Services Administration (GSA) at the forefront of modernizing federal government IT by providing next gen products and services.
sectors.government_public_sector.note: Graded 'yes' on the published framework test rather than the named customer test. Lumen holds the GSA Enterprise Infrastructure Solutions contract vehicle and its EIS page explicitly lists both SD-WAN and SASE among the services delivered under it. This is reinforced by a full dedicated public sector structure: separate Federal, Defense and Intelligence Community, State and Local, Public Safety and Higher Education pages, each mapping SD-WAN and SASE. Recorded caveat: the federal page's own case studies are anonymised ('Federal law enforcement agency', 'Federal infrastructure customer'), so no named agency customer was found. This is US federal and US state and local evidence only, with nothing found for UK or other non-US public sectors.

sectors.education.quote: The University of Denver unlocked digital transformation with reliable network infrastructure from Lumen to power innovation.
sectors.education.note: Dedicated Higher Education page that explicitly frames the product under comparison for campus use ('Learn how a SASE framework with solutions like SD-WAN can help you keep your campus connected'), with two named customers: University of Denver and Link Oregon. The quoted string is the University of Denver entry. Corroborated indirectly by the Walsh Gallegos story, a law firm whose practice is serving educational institutions, and by 'State of New Mexico Statewide Education Network' and 'SABIS Educational Systems' appearing on the customer wall. Evidence is higher education and US K-12 network focused.

sectors.transport_logistics.quote: Crowley Maritime Corporation is a Florida based supply chain logistics company.
sectors.transport_logistics.note: Graded 'partial' rather than 'yes' on a deliberate reading. Crowley is a genuine named logistics customer with a full case study page, which would normally meet the named-case-study test. It was held at 'partial' because the solutions listed for Crowley are Professional Security Services, Networking Solutions, Cloud and Database Management and DIA, and neither SD-WAN nor SASE appears anywhere in that story. There is no dedicated transport or logistics industry page (checked source 14). Rio Metro Regional Transit District, Arctic Glacier and Unical Aviation appear on the customer wall but with testimonials only, no product attribution.

sectors.professional_services.quote: Security and productivity are critical for any law firm, especially one handling sensitive data for educational institutions.
sectors.professional_services.note: Meets the named-case-study test cleanly and specifically for the product under comparison. The Walsh Gallegos law firm story lists 'Lumen SD-WAN and Lumen SASE Solutions for added network visibility and resilience' in its solutions section, and the story is one of only three customer stories featured on the main SASE product page (alongside Ames Construction and United Direct Solutions). Note there is no dedicated professional services industry page; the grade rests on the case study. Troutman Pepper Locke, North Highland and Huitt-Zollars also appear on the customer wall without product attribution.

sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: Held at 'partial' on two grounds. First, although SYNQ3 is featured on the SD-WAN product page under 'Creating convenience in the restaurant industry with bandwidth and innovation', the SYNQ3 story itself names only Dedicated Internet Access, IP VPN and Contact Center Solutions, with no SD-WAN or SASE mention. Second, SYNQ3 is a technology provider selling into restaurants rather than a hospitality operator, so it is weak evidence of hospitality sector delivery. No dedicated hospitality industry page exists (checked source 14). Space Needle appears on the retail page under 'Transforming guest experiences' and Little Rock Convention and Visitors Bureau appears on the customer wall, both without SD-WAN or SASE attribution.

regions.uk_ireland.quote: Extend your service reach to EMEA and Canada locations and endpoints
regions.uk_ireland.note: No UK or Ireland specific coverage, PoP or availability statement was found anywhere. The grade rests entirely on UK and Ireland falling inside the generic 'EMEA' reach claimed in the SASE FAQ, and that claim is doubly qualified: it applies only to customers sold with a US headquarters, and Lumen divested its entire EMEA business to Colt Technology Services on 1 November 2023 (source 24), retaining only 'a small team of talented Lumen employees' there. Supporting negative checks: no en-gb locale site exists (source 31 returned 404) and the locale selector on the Asia Pacific site lists only Australia, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Singapore and the United States, with no UK or European option. A UK-headquartered buyer should treat this as reach-into rather than in-region delivery.

regions.europe.quote: US-sold (HQ in the US) customers can deploy SASE premise-based services across Canada and EMEA locations.
regions.europe.note: Explicitly partial, not 'yes', and the qualifier is the whole story: European delivery is available only to customers sold with a US headquarters and in US currency. The SASE page states separately that 'Global locations are available to customers sold with U.S. headquarters and U.S. currency only at this time.' This is consistent with the November 2023 divestiture of the EMEA business to Colt (source 24). Conflict recorded and not resolved, per instruction: the SD-WAN data sheet (source 7) claims unqualified 'Global availability' for three of four SD-WAN platform options, which sits awkwardly against the SASE FAQ's explicit enumeration and the US-HQ restriction. Also note the SASE FAQ states 'Lumen SASE with VMware offers cloud service availability to EMEA using VMware SASE hosted gateways', i.e. the European cloud gateway capability is the platform vendor's, not Lumen's.

regions.north_america.quote: Lumen hosted gateways for Versa and Fortinet are only available across the six U.S. regions.
regions.north_america.note: The clear home region and the only one with infrastructure-level specificity. Lumen operates its own hosted SASE gateways across six US regions, quotes pricing in US dollars, sells the service to US-headquartered customers as the default case, and every identifiable named customer found across all industry and case study pages is US-based. Canada is explicitly included in the SASE service reach alongside the US. The EMEA divestiture release reinforces the North American centre of gravity, noting Lumen 'will remain a key strategic partner for Colt's customers' needs in North America', i.e. the retained partnership flows inbound to North America.

regions.asia_pacific.quote: Not all products and services are available in all regions and countries; please contact a representative near you for details.
regions.asia_pacific.note: Graded unknown after specific effort to find otherwise, and the negative result is itself informative. The most geographically detailed source (the SASE FAQ, source 6) enumerates service availability as the US, Canada and EMEA, and does not mention Asia Pacific at all. Lumen does run locale sites for Australia, Hong Kong, India, Japan and Singapore, but per the brief a locale site is a website language and not service delivery evidence: the Singapore and India SD-WAN pages (sources 21, 22) carry only a sales phone number and the quoted availability disclaimer, with no coverage, PoP or availability statement, and the Singapore case study index (source 23) is identical to the US one with no Asia Pacific customer. Conflict recorded and not resolved: the SD-WAN data sheet claims unqualified 'Global availability', which contradicts the SASE FAQ's US/Canada/EMEA enumeration. A buyer needing Asia Pacific SASE delivery should treat this as an open question for the supplier.

regions.middle_east_africa.quote: Lumen SASE Solutions management systems are deployed in a redundant cloud environment with regional diversity across a global footprint with site and service availability across EMEA and Canada for US-sold businesses.
regions.middle_east_africa.note: Lowest confidence grade in this set. No Middle East or Africa specific evidence of any kind was found: no country, no PoP, no customer, no locale site. The grade rests solely on the M and A of the acronym 'EMEA' in the quoted sentence, which is thin, and it carries the same two qualifiers as Europe: US-sold customers only, and Lumen divested the EMEA business to Colt in November 2023. In practice the EMEA reach claim appears oriented to European branch locations of US multinationals. Treat as effectively unverified for the Middle East and Africa specifically.

regions.latin_america.quote: Lumen Technologies (NYSE: LUMN) said today it has officially closed the sale of its Latin American operations to Stonepeak for $2.7 billion cash.
regions.latin_america.note: High confidence in the unknown grade because there is positive evidence of absence rather than merely missing evidence. Lumen sold its entire Latin American business to Stonepeak on 1 August 2022; that business now trades independently as Cirion Technologies. Consistent with this, the SASE FAQ's availability enumeration (US, Canada, EMEA) omits Latin America entirely, there is no Latin American locale site, and no Latin American customer was found on any case study page. Buyers requiring Latin American delivery should expect a partner or carrier arrangement, though no such arrangement was published anywhere I looked.

regions.china_mainland.quote: Not all products and services are available in all regions and countries; please contact a representative near you for details.
regions.china_mainland.note: No evidence of any kind for mainland China. No ICP licence, no China-specific arrangement, no China PoP and no China customer were found. Per the brief's guidance, the generic claims found elsewhere were treated as evidence of nothing here: the SD-WAN data sheet's 'Global availability', the network map page's 'spanning 5 continents' (which names no continents and is disclaimed as 'representative of our networks but in general terms'), and the SASE page's '6,300+ unique interconnects globally' are all non-specific. Note that a Hong Kong locale site exists but Hong Kong is not mainland China and would not satisfy a mainland licensing requirement. The SD-WAN service schedule adds that services outside the US may require a separate local country addendum with a local Lumen affiliate, and that services are subject to US export control and economic sanctions law.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.quote: Lumen SASE is a cloud-based network and security experience designed for today's distributed enterprise that is centrally controlled, fully converged and flexibly managed.
organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: Explicit and unambiguous primary target. The SASE page invites buyers to 'Explore next-gen connectivity and security solutions for your large, distributed enterprise' and the SD-WAN page positions 'fully managed or co-managed SD-WAN solutions for enterprise'. Backed by product design: multi-site branch, campus, data centre and colocation management, and site minimums of 10 locations on most SD-WAN platform options. One caveat on the word 'global' in this category: the enterprise targeting is real, but delivery outside the US, Canada and EMEA is unevidenced, so this is better read as large US-headquartered enterprise with international branch reach than as a fully global enterprise proposition.

organisation_fit.mid_market.quote: Discover how to achieve speed, scale and security for your midsize business with resources and product recommendations.
organisation_fit.mid_market.note: Explicitly targeted with a dedicated content path on the SASE page, not merely implied. Reinforced by a second statement on the same page offering connectivity 'for midsize to large businesses', and by published per-location pricing, which is a mid-market buying signal since it lets a smaller buyer size the deal without a bid process. Product-side support is mixed: most SD-WAN platform options carry a 10-site minimum, though the Cisco Meraki option is listed with 'No minimum', which lowers the entry barrier for smaller multi-site estates.

organisation_fit.small_business.quote: Services not available everywhere. Business customers only.
organisation_fit.small_business.note: No SD-WAN or SASE product tier, pricing or case study aimed at small business was found. The evidence points away from it rather than toward it: the SD-WAN page positions the product 'for enterprise', the SASE page's smallest named segment is 'midsize business', most SD-WAN platform options require a 10-site minimum, and the published SASE entry point of $155 per location per month on a 12-month term is priced per site rather than per organisation. A dedicated small business URL was tested and returned 404 (source 32). Graded unknown rather than not_primary because Lumen nowhere explicitly states that small business is out of scope, and the quoted 'Business customers only' line excludes consumers rather than small firms.

published_pricing.quote: starting at $155 per location, per month
published_pricing.note: Unusually well evidenced for this market, which mostly publishes nothing. Lumen publishes actual list entry pricing on its SASE page: $155 per location per month for the Fortinet option and $168 per location per month for the Versa option, both on a 12-month term, with Zero Trust Network Access added at 'Starting at $5 per user' or 'Starting at $9 per user' depending on platform. Graded 'mid' rather than 'value' or 'premium' because these are carrier-managed SASE list prices bundling appliance, security stack and management, which sits in the middle of the managed SASE range rather than at either extreme. Two caveats for a buyer modelling total cost: these are starting prices for the SASE component only and exclude the underlying access circuits, and the SD-WAN product pages and data sheets publish no pricing at all, so an SD-WAN-only comparison has no published anchor.
